title: Thieboudienne
subtitle: Senegalese one-pot rice and fish
excerpt: Thieboudienne is Senegal's national dish -- fish and vegetables cooked in a spiced tomato sauce, with rice cooked in the same pot to absorb all the flavour. It is considered one of the foundational dishes of West African cooking. The result is a deeply coloured, rich, and aromatic rice dish.
sourceNotes: Thieboudienne -- also spelled ceebu jen -- means rice and fish in Wolof, the main language of Senegal. It is considered the national dish of Senegal and has been recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage. It developed in the city of Saint-Louis in the 19th century and spread across West Africa.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The fish stuffing and tomato base can be prepared 1 day ahead. Assemble and cook the rice on the day.

content.text: Traditionally the fish is stuffed with a herb paste before cooking. This version uses a simplified stuffing of garlic and parsley. Use a firm fish -- cod holds together better than flaky varieties during the long cooking time.

items.prepNote: 1 finely chopped for the base, 1 blended with the tomatoes
3 finely chopped for the base, 2 for the fish stuffing
use red palm oil if available
finely chopped -- for the fish stuffing and to serve

content.text: Mix 2 cloves of garlic with half the parsley and a pinch of salt. Make slits in the fish pieces and push a little of the stuffing into each slit.
Heat the oil in a very large pot over medium-high heat. Fry the stuffed fish portions for 3 minutes per side until lightly coloured. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, cook the chopped onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add the 3 remaining cloves of garlic and the tomato puree. Cook for 3 minutes.
Blend the tinned tomatoes with 1 roughly chopped onion. Pour into the pot. Cook for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and dark.
Pour in the fish stock. Add the carrots, cabbage wedges, green pepper, and remaining salt. Bring to the boil. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the fish to the pot. Simmer for 8 minutes. Remove the fish and vegetables carefully and set aside. Keep warm.

Measure the remaining broth -- you need about 700ml for 500g of rice. Add more stock or water if needed. Bring to the boil, add the rinsed rice, stir once, then cover tightly and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes. Pile the rice onto a large platter and arrange the fish and vegetables on top. Scatter with parsley.

items.cause: Insufficient broth or lid lifted during cooking
items.fix: Measure the broth carefully -- you need a 1.4:1 ratio of liquid to rice; do not lift the lid

items.cause: Cooked in the pot for too long
items.fix: Remove the fish as soon as it is just cooked; it only needs 8 minutes simmering

items.cause: Tomato base was not reduced enough
items.fix: Cook the tomato and onion base until it is very thick and dark before adding the stock

content.text: Thieboudienne is considered the national dish of Senegal and one of the greatest rice dishes in the world. It originated in Saint-Louis, the old colonial capital, and spread across Senegal and the Gambia. It is traditionally eaten communally from a large bowl placed on a mat. Each diner takes from the section of the bowl nearest to them.
